title: API resource always includes the customer key, lazily loading it per response
business_context: LedgerFlow exposes invoices through a JSON API consumed by a mobile app and third-party integrations. The serialization contract is explicit and frozen: the 'customer' key is present in an invoice response ONLY when the controller eagerly loaded the customer (the ?include=customer query parameter), and responses never trigger queries of their own. The API was documented against this exact shape.
user_request: While reviewing response payloads for the API changelog, one integrator noticed the invoice payload has grown: a 'customer' key now appears in every response even though the API documentation says it is include-only, and our APM shows an extra query per invoice response. Align the invoice resource with the documented serialization contract: the customer key must appear exactly when the controller included it and never trigger queries of their own.

intentional_defect.summary: InvoiceResource dereferences $this->customer unconditionally: the 'customer' key is always present and every response lazy-loads the relation — a per-response query and a contract violation.
intentional_defect.root_cause: whenLoaded() is the only correct way to conditionally include a relation key; dereferencing the relation directly defeats the conditional and couples the resource to the controller's query plan.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: The output looks correct (the customer data IS accurate), the response is 200, and the visible test asserts the included case — where the key legitimately appears.

non_obvious_invariant: The serialization contract: the 'customer' key is present iff the controller eagerly loaded the customer, and resources never issue queries of their own (responses are projection-only).
expected_diagnosis: The agent must recognize that dereferencing the relation inside the resource both always-includes the key and lazy-loads it per response, and switch to whenLoaded() — preserving the ?include=customer behavior.
safe_fix_constraints: The ?include=customer behavior keeps working (key present with customer data).
Without the include parameter the customer key must be absent from the response.
Resources never trigger queries: no lazy loading inside serialization.
failure_explanation: Every invoice response runs an extra customers SELECT (an N+1 amplifier on list endpoints), and the API drifts from its documentation: integrators that assert the documented shape (customer is include-only) break, and payloads leak the customer block where the docs promise it will not appear.
